title: Momentum as mass times signed velocity
prereq: PH01 signed velocity, speed and SI units; PH02 inertial reference frames.
goals: Calculate signed momentum for a body and a multi-body system.
Compare momentum and kinetic energy without conflating signs.
Recognise the frame and external impulse required for a conservation claim.

sections.heading: Choose a direction and a reference frame
sections.body: Momentum measures directed motion: p = mv. In a 1D laboratory frame with right positive, a 4 kg body travelling left at 2 m/s has p = −8 kg·m/s. State both the mass and signed velocity in the same frame. Units are kg·m/s, equivalent to N·s.

sections.heading: Momentum adds with signs
sections.body: System momentum is the algebraic sum of every body's signed mv. Opposite signed momenta can cancel even when both bodies are moving. A system total of zero does not mean each body is at rest.

sections.heading: Energy answers a different question
sections.body: Translational kinetic energy K = ½mv² is never negative; the speed is squared. Reverse an arrow and the momentum reverses, but the kinetic energy stays the same. Equal momentum does not imply equal kinetic energy, and equal kinetic energy need not imply equal momentum.

sections.heading: What is actually conserved?
sections.body: In a fixed chosen system, momentum changes by NET external impulse. Momentum can be calculated at any instant without asserting conservation. Before carrying it across an interaction, inspect all external forces and the time interval.

worked.name: Foundation · leftward cart
worked.setup: A 4 kg cart travels at −2 m/s.
worked.check: Its momentum points left; its kinetic energy is positive.

worked.name: Connected · equal momentum, unequal energy
worked.setup: Two carts have 2 kg at +3 m/s and 6 kg at +1 m/s.
steps: Thus equal p does not imply equal K.
worked.check: Heavier carts can have the same p at a lower speed.

worked.name: Transfer · equal energy, different momentum
worked.setup: Compare 1 kg at +6 m/s and 4 kg at +3 m/s.
steps: Both have 18 J of kinetic energy.
Squaring in K loses direction information, so keep signed momentum separately.
worked.check: A larger mass at the same K has a larger momentum magnitude.

trap.wrong: Add magnitudes of opposite-direction velocities, or assign negative kinetic energy.
trap.repair: Draw right/left signs before summing mv; calculate each positive ½mv² separately.

assumptions: Velocities use one common inertial frame.
Conservation requires an isolated system or explicitly accounted external impulse.

model.label: Teaching model: velocity of a 2 kg cart

prompt.stem: Two carts at one instant: A has mass 2 kg moving RIGHT at +3 m/s; B has mass 3 kg moving LEFT at −1 m/s. Using the same laboratory frame, find total signed momentum and total kinetic energy.
prompt.prediction: Which direction does the combined momentum point? Explain before computing.
prompt.boundaryPrompt: Changed condition: double BOTH signed velocities, holding masses and directions fixed. Recompute momentum and kinetic energy.
